title: CHEAP Chinese Carbon Bike Frame - In-depth Review (Elves Falath Pro 2022) | Part 2

takeaways.text: Custom two-tone chameleon paint (with his name) was included for about £800; he rated the finish 10/10 with only a very slight lip at the colour join.

Calipers on the BB86 shell read 86.4–86.6 mm wide and 40.7–40.9 mm bore (41 mm nominal); upper headset seat 51.9–52.3 mm and lower seat more variable (about 50.6–52.2 mm) for 52 mm bearings, which still pressed in.
Braze-on front derailleur mount, Di2-ready, pre-installed internal guide tubes and a spare hanger; the aero seatpost comes with grip paper and textured clamping faces to resist slipping.
His frame weighed 860 g and the fork 425 g with thru-axle (frame size not stated); Elves' current reference is 1,080 g for a size 46, so the two are not directly comparable.
A five-year global warranty card came with the 2022 frameset.

disclosure: The creator reviews his own Falath Pro Disc 2022 frameset; the description links a third-party spec page and mentions no sponsorship.
summary: Owner inspection of a custom-painted Falath Pro Disc 2022 frameset: paint, bottom-bracket and headset bore measurements, derailleur mounts, cable routing, the shaped seatpost with grip tape, the weighed frame and fork, and the warranty card.
